- Expansion to add 450 guest rooms and a luxury indoor water experience - 

NASHVILLE, Tenn., Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Ryman Hospitality Properties, Inc. (NYSE: RHP) (the “Company”), a leading lodging and hospitality real estate investment trust (“REIT”) specializing in group-oriented, upscale convention center resorts and entertainment experiences, today announced plans to add 450 guest rooms, a luxury indoor water experience and a multi-story parking structure to its Gaylord Rockies Resort & Convention Center in Aurora, Colorado. The planned expansion will increase the resort’s guest rooms to 1,951, making it the third-largest Gaylord Hotels property by room count.

Mark Fioravanti, President and Chief Executive Officer of Ryman Hospitality Properties, said, “Since we opened reservations at Gaylord Rockies, group demand has increasingly exceeded the resort’s available room supply. From 2023 through 2025, we turned down approximately 38% of large-group room nights at the lead stage due to capacity constraints. This expansion will allow us to capture that demand and bring more of our largest Gaylord Hotels customers to Colorado.”

Modeled after SoundWaves at Gaylord Opryland, the year-round indoor luxury water experience is expected to span approximately 110,000 square feet. The water experience is expected to feature a slide tower with seven rides, including a mat racer and a tube slide complex; a wave pool; an adventure river; a kids’ activity area with a multi-level play structure, toddler slide, spray ground and dump bucket; a 144-seat restaurant; and 15 private indoor cabanas.

Designed to accommodate future growth, Gaylord Rockies has the meeting space and food and beverage offerings to support the additional rooms. The expansion is the latest phase of a multiphase capital investment program at Colorado’s largest combined resort and convention center, which has undergone approximately $100 million in enhancements since 2022.

Completed projects since 2022 include:

  • The 2024 addition of the Mountain View Pavilion along with lawn and landscaping enhancements.
  • A transformational renovation of the resort’s Grand Lodge, including the debut of The Fortunate Prospector and Embers Lodge Bar outlets.
  • A re-concepting of the resort’s food and beverage program, including the addition of Garden+Grain Seasonal Kitchen and Copper Table, a redesigned Old Hickory Steakhouse and an enhanced Mountain Pass Sports Bar.

Fioravanti concluded, “Our continued investment in this property reflects our belief that Gaylord Rockies is on track to become one of the most successful non-gaming convention center hotels in the United States. Since its opening, approximately 75% of group production has come from groups that were new to Colorado, and we look forward to attracting even more visitors to this stunning region in the years ahead. We are thankful to our operating partners at Marriott, the state of Colorado, the city of Aurora and the Aurora Economic Development Council for sharing our vision.”

Preconstruction site work is scheduled to begin in December 2026, and the rooms are expected to be completed during Q1 of 2029, with the indoor water experience expected to be completed in late 2029. The Weitz Company will serve as general contractor for the $305 million project, which is expected to be funded with cash on hand and borrowings under the Company’s credit facility.

About Ryman Hospitality Properties, Inc.

Ryman Hospitality Properties, Inc. (NYSE: RHP) is a leading lodging and hospitality real estate investment trust that specializes in group-oriented, upscale convention center resorts and entertainment experiences. The Company’s holdings include Gaylord Opryland Resort & Convention Center; Gaylord Palms Resort & Convention Center; Gaylord Texan Resort & Convention Center; Gaylord National Resort & Convention Center; and Gaylord Rockies Resort & Convention Center, five of the top seven largest non-gaming convention center hotels in the United States based on total indoor meeting space. The Company also owns the Grande Lakes Orlando Resort, the JW Marriott Phoenix Desert Ridge Resort & Spa and the JW Marriott San Antonio Hill Country Resort & Spa as well as two ancillary hotels adjacent to the Company’s Gaylord Hotels properties. The Company’s hotel portfolio is managed by Marriott International and includes a combined total of 13,956 rooms as well as more than 3 million square feet of total indoor and outdoor meeting space in top convention and leisure destinations across the country. RHP also owns an approximate 70% controlling ownership interest in Opry Entertainment Group (OEG), which is composed of entities owning a growing collection of iconic and emerging country music brands, including the Grand Ole Opry; Ryman Auditorium; WSM 650 AM; Ole Red; Category 10; Nashville-area attractions; and Block 21, a mixed-use entertainment, lodging, office and retail complex, including the W Austin Hotel and the ACL Live at the Moody Theater, located in downtown Austin, Texas. OEG manages select outdoor live music venues, including Ascend Federal Credit Union Amphitheater in Nashville and CCNB Amphitheatre in Simpsonville, South Carolina. OEG also owns a majority interest in Southern Entertainment, a leading festival and events business. RHP operates OEG as its Entertainment segment in a taxable REIT subsidiary, and its results are consolidated in the Company’s financial results.

VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / November 19, 2026 / Gamma Resources Ltd (TSX-V:GAMA)(OTCQB:GAMXF)(Frankfurt:MRD0) ("Gamma" or the "Company") is pleased to announce the expansion of its Mesa Arc property in Rio Arriba County, New Mexico. The Company has added an additional 12 claims to its mineral tenure. The new claims are in addition to the 185 lode claims previously announced in the Company's July 31, 2025 press release ("Gamma Resources Expands Uranium Holdings in New Mexico's Chamma Basin") and bring the Mesa Arc claim package to approximately 4,760 acres. The Company has completed its radon flux baseline survey with results and interpretation pending.

The Mesa Arc Project now comprises 238 lode mining claims, consisting of the 197 claims staked by the Company and the 41 previously leased claims. The newly added claims are contiguous with the Company's existing claim block and immediately adjacent to the Company's AR-15 area.

The Mesa Arc Project covers a four-mile trend of historically documented uranium mineralization within the Chama Basin of northern New Mexico (see "About the Mesa Arc Project" and "Note Regarding Historical Estimates" below).

"Although small, the claims lie immediately south of the AR-15 area, their addition further expands Gamma's ground within the historically identified mineralized trend." Said Connor Messler, President and Chief Executive Officer of Gamma Resources Ltd.

The claim expansion is consistent with Gamma's strategy of building a U.S.-based uranium exploration portfolio at a time of growing demand for domestic, responsibly sourced uranium supply.

Radon Flux Baseline Survey

The Company has completed its radon flux baseline survey previously announced in the Company's November 10, 2026 press release (titled "Gamma Resources Announces Planned Radon Flux Baseline Survey at Mesa Arc Uranium Project in New Mexico, Provides Update on Project Timelines"). With 250 readings taken from the Company's AR-30 area. Data collected during the survey is currently being processed, with results expected in the coming weeks.

Gamma Resources Ltd claim block (green), with the newly announced claims (red). The radon flux baseline survey was completed targeting the Company's AR-30 target area.

About the Mesa Arc Project

The Mesa Arc Project covers a four-mile trend of historically documented uranium mineralizations within the Chama Basin of northern New Mexico. Following a recent claim expansion, the property comprises 238 lode mining claims covering approximately 4,760 acres. The project has seen extensive exploration work with roughly 1,000 drill holes completed on, and adjacent to, the Mesa Arc property between the 1960s and 1980s. Of these, 406 holes are located within the current claim block; mineralization on adjacent ground is not necessarily indicative of mineralization on the property. A historical estimate for the AR-15 area in Section 10, T25N R5E, is reported in "Martinez Canyon Project, Rio Arriba County, NM - Resource Calculation," prepared by J.R. Carden for Magnum Uranium Corp. and dated June 30, 2006. Mr. Carden is currently an advisor to the Company. Using the surface polygonal method on 85 historical drill holes, the report estimated a "Total Resource," with no cut-off grade applied, of 329,700 tons grading 0.106% U₃O₈ containing approximately 701,700 pounds of U₃O₈. The report also defined a high-grade core within the Total Resource, using a cut-off of 5 feet at 0.10% U₃O₈, of 154,700 tons grading 0.15% U₃O₈ containing approximately 474,500 pounds of U₃O₈; this is a subset of, and is not additional to, the Total Resource. Polygons were drawn around each mineralized hole with sides at half the distance to the nearest hole or extended approximately 75 feet where no bounding hole existed. Grades are equivalent uranium (eU₃O₈) from down-hole gamma probing, converted to U₃O₈ using a disequilibrium factor of eU₃O₈ × 1.29 − 0.001, and a tonnage factor of 16 cubic feet per ton was used. The terms "Total Resource" and "resource" used in the report do not correspond to the mineral resource or mineral reserve categories of the CIM Definition Standards. The Company considers the historical estimate relevant because the AR-15 area lies entirely within the current Mesa Arc claim block. Its reliability is limited because it relies on Anaconda drill logs and maps from the 1970s, the drill hole locations were reconstructed from a 1979 survey map not tied to topography, the grades are probe-derived equivalents adjusted by a disequilibrium factor that the report recommended be refined, and the original drill data are held by Anaconda and ARCO, with the Company relying on copies of the archived logs. The Company is not aware of any more recent estimates or data. To verify the historical estimate or upgrade it to a current mineral resource, the Company would need to compile and validate the historical drill data, complete confirmation and twin drilling with chemical assays to test the disequilibrium factor, and have a qualified person prepare a new mineral resource estimate. A qualified person has not done sufficient work to classify the historical estimate as current mineral resources or mineral reserves, and the Company is not treating the historical estimate as current mineral resources or mineral reserves.

As of October 2026 the Company has withdrawn the draft plan of operations previously under review by the United States Forest Service. The draft, initially submitted in the first quarter of 2026, has been withdrawn as the Company develops its exploration targeting strategy.

About Gamma Resources Ltd.

Gamma Resources Ltd. (TSX-V:GAMA)(OTCQB:GAMXF)(FRA:MRD0) is a U.S.-focused uranium exploration company advancing high-quality assets in the Mountain West region of the United States. The Company's portfolio includes the Green River Project in Utah, comprising 1,100 acres near prominent regional producers, and the Mesa Arc Project in New Mexico, a strategic land position now totaling 4,760 acres that hosts a historical uranium estimate in the Chama Basin. Management believes the Company is well-positioned to benefit from the policy and market tailwinds reshaping the U.S. nuclear landscape and to help meet growing demand with responsibly sourced, U.S.-based uranium supply.

Gamma trades on the TSX Venture Exchange (TSX-V: GAMA), in the United States on the OTCQB (OTCQB: GAMXF), and in Germany on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (FRA: MRD0).

Qualified Person

Anders Hogrelius (PG, RPGeo, SME-RM, MAIG), a Qualified Person as defined by National Instrument 43-101, has reviewed and approved the scientific and technical information in this news release. Mr. Hogrelius is an independent consultant to the Company. Mr. Hogrelius has reviewed the historical drill logs and reports underlying the historical estimate, including the June 30, 2006 Carden report and the Anaconda records it cites. The historical sampling and analytical data cannot be independently verified, as the original samples are no longer available and the historical drill holes have been backfilled and cannot be re-probed, and the historical estimate should be read with that limitation in mind.

Note Regarding Historical Estimates

The uranium estimate figures referred to in this news release are historical estimates. A qualified person has not done sufficient work to classify these historical estimates as current mineral resources or mineral reserves, the Company is not treating them as current mineral resources or mineral reserves, and they should not be relied upon as such.

Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Critical One Energy Inc. (CSE: CRTL) (OTCQB: CTLOF) (FSE: 4EF) ("Critical One" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that its co-development partner, Solar International Core Canada ("SICC"), has engaged Process Research ORTECH Inc. ("PRO/ORTECH"), under which PRO/ORTECH will provide metallurgical services to advance Ontario antimony processing.

The engagement of PRO/ORTECH marks a further step in advancing Critical One's previously announced binding memorandum of understanding ("MOU") with SICC (see news release dated October 29, 2026). To support this work, Critical One has delivered selected HQ drill-core samples from its flagship Howells Lake Antimony-Gold Project ("Howells Lake") to PRO/ORTECH's facility in Mississauga, Ontario.

Located in the homelands of the Eabametoong First Nation, Thunder Bay Mining Division, Howells Lake is approximately 120 kilometres west of the Ring of Fire access corridor in northwestern Ontario, Canada.

Highlights:

  • SICC-PRO/ORTECH arrangement: The engagement brings PRO/ORTECH into the partnership as the metallurgical services provider for the Ontario facility being developed by Northlink Development Group Inc. ("Northlink").

  • Recovery and refining: PRO/ORTECH will evaluate antimony recovery and potential processing options for producing antimony trisulphide (Sb₂S₃) and/or antimony trioxide (Sb₂O₃) products.

  • Howells Lake samples delivered: Approximately 100 kilograms of selected HQ drill core from a five-hole, 789-metre metallurgical drilling program have been delivered to PRO/ORTECH for evaluation.

"Engaging Process Research ORTECH is a critical milestone in building an end-to-end domestic antimony supply chain in Ontario," said Babak Arefpour, Chief Executive Officer of Solar International Core Canada Ltd. "In discussions with government, the pairing of Critical One's high-grade Howells Lake feedstock with PRO/ORTECH's world-class metallurgical expertise and Northlink's development leadership, SICC is committed to advancing the technical foundation required to bring strategic mineral processing capacity online in Canada."

"Progressing our MOU with SICC is both visionary and extraordinary," said Duane Parnham, Executive Chairman and CEO of Critical One Energy. "By integrating mining, processing and offtake under one strategic partnership, we are creating lasting value for our shareholders, the Eabametoong First Nation, and North America's industrial and defence needs."

Shareholder and Investor Webinar - November 19, 2026

Critical One will host a live webinar on November 19, 2026, at 11:30 a.m. Eastern Time, giving its shareholders and prospective investors an opportunity to hear directly from the partners advancing the Company's Canadian antimony supply chain strategy.

Duane Parnham of Critical One will be joined by Marc Kealey of SICC, Perry Kotsopoulos of Northlink, and Jonathan Chen of PRO/ORTECH. The discussion will cover progress under the MOU, the financing commitments, metallurgical work on Howells Lake samples, and the planned course of action.

The 15-minute presentation will be followed by an audience question-and-answer (Q&A) session.

Register to attend: https://my.demio.com/ref/Xz6cz9CqxrpCR8lU

Process Research ORTECH and the Ontario Processing Initiative

PRO/ORTECH is a Canadian process development company with a 40,000-square-foot laboratory and pilot plant in Mississauga, specializing in mineral processing, hydrometallurgy and pyrometallurgy. Its team includes Dr. Sankar Das Gupta, Chief Chemist and Managing Director and co-founder of Electrovaya Inc.; and Jonathan Chen, Chief Executive Officer.

PRO/ORTECH's work is intended to provide the process data for the plant's design. Under Critical One's previously announced MOU with SICC, Northlink is the proposed facility's developer and project manager, and Critical One is positioned as a future feedstock supplier and carried equity partner, subject to the MOU's terms and conditions (see news release dated October 29, 2026).

On November 12, 2026, representatives of Critical One, Northlink and SICC visited PRO/ORTECH's facility to inspect Howells Lake samples received the previous day and discuss the proposed metallurgical evaluation (see Figure 1).

Figure 1. From left to right, Marc Kealey (SICC), Perry Kotsopoulos (Northlink) and Duane Parnham (Critical One Energy) review Howells Lake HQ antimony drill core and sample material at Process Research ORTECH in Mississauga, Ontario on November 12, 2026.

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:
https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/12034/324833_3ae921ddb488f826_001full.jpg

Metallurgical Samples and Proposed Test Work

The samples are whole HQ core, 63.5 millimetres in diameter, from a metallurgical-drill program completed in October 2026. They were selected to represent disseminated, vein-hosted, semi-massive and massive stibnite, the main antimony mineral at Howells Lake (Figure 2).

The work follows a preliminary mineralogical study by Blue Coast Research Ltd. In the four samples examined, that study found antimony hosted mainly in stibnite, measured liberation after grinding of 92.8% to 99.1% for stibnite and 84.9% to 89.7% for berthierite, a second antimony mineral, and identified no arsenic- or mercury-bearing minerals (see news release dated July 27, 2026).

The proposed metallurgical program includes scoping and bench-scale evaluation of gravity concentration, flotation, and stibnite leaching to assess recovery and potential antimony trisulphide (Sb₂S₃) and/or antimony trioxide (Sb₂O₃) products.



Figure 2. HQ drill core from Howells Lake. Left: sericite-silica altered porphyry crosscut by a quartz vein (top row) in contact with massive stibnite downhole (bottom row), at 79 metres in HQ-2026-002. Right: cross-section of HQ drill core with semi-massive stibnite within a quartz vein.

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:
https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/12034/324833_3ae921ddb488f826_002full.jpg

Next Steps

The parties will confirm the initial scope, schedule, and deliverables for the metallurgical program. Critical One will report material results as available. Drilling continues toward an initial mineral resource estimate at Howells Lake, with assays pending (see news release dated November 9, 2026).

About Process Research ORTECH Inc.

Process Research ORTECH Inc. (PRO/ORTECH) is a Mississauga, Ontario process development company serving the mining, metallurgical, recycling and chemical industries. Additional information is available at www.processortech.com.

About Solar International Core Canada

Solar International Core Canada (SICC) is a strategic capital partner with tier-one institutional financial capacity and sovereign wealth relationships, including institutional financing partnerships with the Sultanate of Oman Sovereign Wealth Fund.

About Northlink Development Group Inc.

Northlink Development Group Inc. is a Canadian development company focused on critical minerals, infrastructure and energy projects. It brings together stakeholders, capital and delivery partners to advance projects and strengthen domestic supply chains. Additional information is available at www.northlinkdevelopment.ca.

About Critical One Energy Inc.

Critical One Energy Inc. is a critical minerals exploration company dedicated to advancing its flagship Howells Lake Antimony-Gold Project as a new North American source of antimony for defence, energy storage, industrial applications, and high-performance technologies such as data centres and semiconductors. The Howells Lake Antimony-Gold Project, located in Ontario, Canada, hosts high-grade antimony mineralization confirmed through a modern drilling program. The Company's objective is to advance Howells Lake as a potential Canadian source of antimony and help reduce North America's dependence on foreign supply.

CHICAGO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--NielsenIQ (NYSE: NIQ), a leading consumer intelligence company, today announced that Danny Lange and Chris Tung have been appointed to its Board of Directors, effective Nov. 18, 2026.

Lange brings more than three decades of technology leadership, including senior roles building and scaling artificial intelligence and machine learning capabilities at Google, Unity, Uber, Amazon and Microsoft. Chris brings deep operating experience across Greater China and Asia Pacific, along with a proven track record of using data and technology to build brands and grow businesses. Their perspectives will be important as we execute our strategy, scale new AI offerings including NIQ Optiq and ConnectAI, and help clients grow in a rapidly changing market.”

About Danny Lange

Lange is the founder of Agentimus LLC, an AI advisory firm, where he advises private equity and growth equity investors and their portfolio companies on artificial intelligence. He previously served as Vice President of Business Intelligence and AI at Google, Senior Vice President of Artificial Intelligence at Unity Software, Head of Machine Learning at Uber, and General Manager of Amazon Machine Learning at Amazon. He also held engineering leadership positions at Microsoft. Lange serves on the boards of Trifork Group AG and ZeroNorth A/S. He holds a Master of Science degree and a Ph.D. in computer science from the Technical University of Denmark and is a named inventor on 24 U.S. patents.

“NIQ has a difficult-to-replicate AI advantage: trusted, proprietary AI-ready data grounded in real consumer behavior,” Lange said. “The opportunity now is to make that intelligence usable by the next generation of AI systems and agentic workflows, including agentic commerce. I’m excited to help NIQ turn that advantage into products and platforms that create meaningful value for clients and shareholders.”

About Chris Tung

Tung most recently served as Group Chief Marketing Officer and Chief Executive Officer, China, at Shangri-La Asia Limited. He previously served as President of Alibaba Group, leading strategic development, after serving as the company’s Chief Marketing Officer. Earlier in his career, he was Chief Executive Officer of VML China and held senior leadership roles at PepsiCo China, L’Oréal, GigaMedia and Procter & Gamble. “NIQ has a powerful global perspective on consumer behavior and a significant opportunity to deepen its impact across Asia and around the world,” Tung said. “As an NIQ client during my time at Alibaba, including when I built the Uni Marketing system, I saw firsthand how NIQ’s data can help brands understand consumers and make better decisions. I am pleased to join the Board and support the company as it advances its strategy and strengthens the value it delivers for clients.”

RAHWAY, N.J.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Merck (NYSE: MRK), known as MSD outside of the United States and Canada, and Isomorphic Labs, an AI-first drug design and development company, today announced a research collaboration that brings together Isomorphic Labs’ AI approach to drug discovery with Merck’s rich proprietary data resources and deep discovery experience.

The companies will collaborate to discover therapeutic small molecule candidates against an oncology target of strategic importance. Isomorphic Labs will perform in silico predictions and deliver molecular designs, applying its proprietary drug design engine (IsoDDE) incorporating select high-quality proprietary data sets supplied by Merck for the purpose of this collaboration. Merck will be responsible for preclinical and clinical development, as well as manufacturing and commercialization of any products derived from the collaboration.

Under the terms of the agreement, Isomorphic Labs will receive an upfront payment from Merck and be eligible for payments based on the achievement of specified research, development, regulatory and commercial milestones, as well as tiered royalties on net sales. Isomorphic Labs also receives an option to co-fund development activities in return for elevated royalties.

“The key to successfully leveraging AI/ML for molecular invention lies in close coordination of wet-lab and dry-lab functions,” said George Addona, senior vice president and head of discovery, preclinical development and translational medicine, Merck Research Laboratories. “By combining Merck’s substantial internal data capabilities and discovery expertise with Isomorphic Labs’ powerful modeling and compute capabilities, we aim to identify new ways to design and create better candidates faster.”

“Through this collaboration with Merck, we will apply our world-leading drug design engine to unlock significant discovery progress,” said Sarah Skerratt, chief research officer, Isomorphic Labs. “By leveraging the generative and predictive power of the IsoDDE to address this challenging program, this collaboration highlights our companies’ shared commitment to innovation for the benefit of patient populations with unmet needs.”

The collaboration highlights the transformative power of bringing together advanced AI, unique data sets and established biopharmaceutical leadership to accelerate the advancement of therapeutic candidates, navigating complex biology with unprecedented speed and precision.

Isomorphic Labs was founded in 2021, to transform drug discovery with the power of artificial intelligence, ushering in a new era of biomedical breakthroughs. Key Terms

small moleculemedical
A small molecule is a low-weight chemical compound that can enter cells easily and interact with specific proteins or biological pathways to change how they work, much like a small key fitting into a lock. Investors care because small molecules are a common and often faster route to develop medicines, can be manufactured at scale, and may offer clearer regulatory and commercial paths compared with larger biologic therapies, affecting potential costs, timelines and returns.
in silicotechnical
In silico means using computer models, simulations, or data analysis to study biological, chemical, or financial processes instead of physical experiments. For investors, in silico work can speed up research, lower costs and highlight promising opportunities or risks early—like using a flight simulator to test maneuvers before flying a real plane—while still requiring real-world testing to confirm results.
preclinicalmedical
Preclinical describes the stage of drug or medical-product development when researchers test a candidate in the lab and in animals to see if it is safe, reaches intended targets, and shows basic effectiveness before any human trials begin. For investors, preclinical status signals an early, higher‑risk opportunity where positive lab results can increase value but significant work, time, and regulatory hurdles remain — like proofing a prototype in a workshop before road testing.
tiered royaltiesfinancial
Tiered royalties are a payment structure where the percentage of earnings paid as royalties changes based on different levels of sales or production. For example, a company might pay a smaller percentage on initial sales and a higher percentage as sales increase beyond certain points. This system encourages higher sales by adjusting payments, making it important for investors to understand how revenue sharing may vary as a product or project grows.

Completes Agile Defense acquisition, delivers earnings above guidance, and establishes fiscal year 2027 guidance

TYSONS, Va.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Maximus (NYSE: MMS), a leading provider of government services, reported financial results for the three months and year ended September 30, 2026. The acquisition of Agile Defense, LLC (Agile Defense) was completed on November 18, 2026.

Highlights for fiscal year 2026 include:

  • Full year revenue of $5.23 billion, landing within the guidance range.
  • Full year operating margin of 11.7% and adjusted EBITDA margin of 14.2%, along with diluted earnings per share of $7.27 and adjusted diluted earnings per share of $8.24, which exceeded the top end of guidance and increased 12.0% over the prior year on an adjusted earnings per share basis.
  • Full year cash flows from operating activities of $112 million and free cash flow of $69 million. Subsequent to fiscal year-end, collections totaled more than $330 million from a major customer.
  • Repurchases of Maximus common stock totaling approximately $192 million during fiscal year 2026.
  • Establishes fiscal year 2027 guidance of $5.45 billion to $5.65 billion of revenue, adjusted diluted earnings per share of $7.50 to $8.00, and free cash flow of $700 million to $800 million; fiscal year 2027 guidance reflects the absence of an estimated $1.05 per share of benefit recognized in fiscal year 2026 attributable to a specific program, which is discussed further below.
  • A quarterly cash dividend of $0.33 per share payable on November 30, 2026, to shareholders of record on November 13, 2026.

"Fiscal year 2026 reflected the benefits of disciplined execution, technology-enabled productivity enhancements, and thoughtful capital allocation," said Bruce Caswell, President and Chief Executive Officer. "Throughout the year, we continued deploying automation and AI-enabled solutions across our operations, improving efficiency, strengthening profitability, and delivering meaningful outcomes for customers. These efforts contributed to adjusted diluted earnings per share of $8.24, representing 12.0% growth over the prior year and performance above the top end of our most recently updated guidance range."

Caswell continued, "Subsequent to fiscal year-end, we completed the acquisition of Agile Defense, which significantly expands our position in defense and national security markets and enhances our portfolio of technology-enabled capabilities. As we enter fiscal year 2027, we remain focused on integrating Agile Defense, growing existing customer relationships, executing on opportunities associated with recent policy initiatives, and further advancing our leadership in AI-enabled solutions and technology innovation."

Agile Defense Acquisition Close

On November 18, 2026, Maximus completed its acquisition of Agile Defense, a provider of mission-focused technology solutions supporting customers across the Department of War, Intelligence Community, homeland security, and civilian agencies.

The acquisition expands Maximus' presence in defense and national security markets while adding differentiated capabilities in cybersecurity, digital modernization, software and analytics, cloud solutions, and AI-enabled mission support services. The transaction further diversifies the U.S. Federal Service's portfolio, enhances access to strategically important customers, and increases exposure to attractive markets with favorable long-term growth characteristics.

Agile Defense is expected to contribute approximately ten months of revenue during fiscal year 2027 and is included in the fiscal year 2027 guidance.

Consolidated Fiscal Year 2026 Results

Revenue for fiscal year 2026 was $5.23 billion, compared to $5.43 billion reported for the prior fiscal year. As previously discussed, fiscal year 2025 benefited from elevated natural disaster support activities and temporary clinical program volume surges that did not recur at the same level during fiscal year 2026. Revenue finished within the fiscal year 2026 guidance range and was consistent with our expectations throughout the year.

For fiscal year 2026, the operating margin was 11.7% and adjusted EBITDA margin was 14.2%, compared to 9.7% and 12.9%, respectively, in the prior fiscal year. The improvement reflects technology-enabled productivity enhancements, including automation initiatives, disciplined cost management efforts, and strong operational performance.

Diluted earnings per share were $7.27 and adjusted diluted earnings per share were $8.24 for fiscal year 2026. This compares to $5.51 and $7.36, respectively, in the prior fiscal year. Adjusted diluted earnings per share exceeded the top end of the most recently updated guidance range for fiscal year 2026 and increased 12.0% over the prior year. Earnings growth was driven principally by improved operating performance reflected in the margin improvement and the benefit of capital deployment actions, including share repurchases.

U.S. Federal Services Segment

U.S. Federal Services Segment revenue for fiscal year 2026 was approximately $2.99 billion. Prior fiscal year revenue of $3.07 billion benefited from nearly $100 million of elevated natural disaster support activity and temporary clinical volume surges that did not recur at the same level during fiscal year 2026.

The segment operating margin for fiscal year 2026 was 18.1%, compared to 15.3% reported for the prior fiscal year. Margin expansion was driven by technology-enabled efficiencies, productivity improvements, strong execution across core program areas, and favorable operating leverage generated through automation initiatives deployed throughout the fiscal year. Together, these factors helped create opportunities to efficiently process higher volumes and improve profitability, such as incentive payments on the Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Disability Examination (VA MDE) program during the first three quarters of the fiscal year 2026.

Fourth quarter results of fiscal year 2026 reflected the previously disclosed customer-directed modification to the VA MDE program regarding performance incentives. The fourth quarter also benefited from strong performance across the clinical portfolio, which is expected to moderate in fiscal year 2027.

U.S. Services Segment

U.S. Services Segment revenue for fiscal year 2026 was $1.68 billion, compared to $1.76 billion reported for the prior fiscal year. Revenue performance was generally consistent with expectations and reflected varying volumes across several contract areas. Revenue trends improved throughout fiscal year 2026, culminating in positive organic growth in the fourth quarter.

The segment operating margin for fiscal year 2026 was 9.1%, compared to 9.7% reported in the prior fiscal year. Fiscal year 2026 results included a $6.9 million non-cash impairment charge related to a software asset developed and capitalized for a specific customer.

We continue to see encouraging demand indicators associated with Medicaid community engagement requirements, program integrity activities, eligibility administration, and other state government initiatives that are expected to support future growth opportunities.

Outside the U.S. Segment

Outside the U.S. Segment revenue for fiscal year 2026 was $557 million, compared to $600 million reported for the prior fiscal year. The revenue decrease was attributable to previously divested businesses as well as lower revenue across several employment services and clinical programs amidst certain customer-specific challenges.

The segment reported a modest operating loss, primarily reflecting the lower revenue across those employment services and clinical programs. Maximus continues to focus on driving profitable growth through disciplined bid selection, operational improvements, and successful conversion of its sales pipeline.

Sales and Pipeline

Signed contract awards for fiscal year 2026 totaled $2.51 billion, and contracts pending (awarded but unsigned) totaled $1.86 billion at September 30, 2026. The book-to-bill ratio at September 30, 2026, was 0.5x on a trailing twelve-month basis and the quarterly book-to-bill ratio improved to approximately 1.0x, representing the strongest quarterly award performance of fiscal year 2026.

The fourth quarter book-to-bill ratio was enabled by a signed contract award for a significant state Medicaid contract renewal representing more than $800 million of total contract value over a ten-year period. Included in the contracts pending balance are two recently awarded state Medicaid contract renewals totaling approximately $528 million of total contract value.

The total sales pipeline at September 30, 2026, was $44.8 billion (comprised of approximately $4.01 billion in proposals pending, $1.61 billion in proposals in preparation, and $39.2 billion in opportunities tracking). New work opportunities represent approximately 61% of the total sales pipeline, and U.S. Federal Services Segment opportunities represent approximately 58% of the total sales pipeline.

During fiscal year 2026, Maximus achieved a recompete win rate of approximately 89%, reflecting the strength of its customer relationships, operational performance, and technology-enabled service delivery model.

Balance Sheet and Cash Flows

At September 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents totaled $280 million, and gross debt was $1.61 billion. The ratio of debt, net of allowed cash, to consolidated EBITDA for the full year ended September 30, 2026, as calculated in accordance with our credit agreement, was 1.8x.

Following the completion of the Agile Defense acquisition, our pro forma leverage ratio is expected to be approximately 2.3x, remaining within Maximus' targeted leverage range of 2x to 3x and preserving financial flexibility for future capital allocation priorities.

For fiscal year 2026, cash flows from operating activities totaled $112 million and free cash flow was $69 million, enabled by $278 million of free cash flow for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. This compares to $429 million and $366 million, respectively, in the prior fiscal year.

Days sales outstanding, or DSO, were 93 days at September 30, 2026, compared to 98 days at June 30, 2026. Subsequent to fiscal year-end and through November 13, 2026, we collected more than $330 million from a major customer that had been anticipated in our fiscal year 2026 guidance. As a result, a portion of cash generation expected during fiscal year 2026 shifted into fiscal year 2027 guidance due to timing-related factors rather than collection concerns. During fiscal year 2026, we repurchased approximately 2.6 million shares of Maximus common stock totaling approximately $192 million. As of November 13, 2026, the full $400 million balance from the most recent Board of Directors authorization remains available.

On October 5, 2026, our Board of Directors declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.33 for each share of our common stock outstanding. The dividend is payable on November 30, 2026, to shareholders of record on November 13, 2026.

Fiscal Year 2027 Guidance

Maximus is establishing fiscal year 2027 guidance.

We expect revenue to range between $5.45 billion and $5.65 billion. The outlook includes approximately ten months of contribution from Agile Defense and reflects expectations for continued growth opportunities across defense and national security markets, state government programs, and technology-enabled services.

Maximus expects adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 12.8% for fiscal year 2027 and adjusted diluted earnings per share to range between $7.50 and $8.00 per share.

This guidance assumes no incentive contribution related to the VA MDE contracts during fiscal year 2027. Fiscal year 2026 included incentive-related revenue and profit equal to an estimated $75 million and $1.05 adjusted earnings per share, respectively, total contribution across the first three quarters of the fiscal year 2026. Excluding the incentive contribution related to the VA MDE contracts to the fiscal year 2026, the midpoint of our adjusted diluted earnings per share guidance represents growth of approximately 8%.

We expect free cash flow to range between $700 million and $800 million. The outlook reflects DSO returning to the historical range of 60-70 days and includes the benefit of collections that shifted beyond fiscal year-end.

For fiscal year 2027, Maximus expects amortization of intangible assets of approximately $96 million, depreciation and amortization of property, equipment and capitalized software of approximately $55 million, interest expense of approximately $110 million, an effective tax rate of approximately 25%, and weighted average shares outstanding of approximately 52.1 million.

Key Terms

adjusted ebitdafinancial
Adjusted EBITDA is a way companies measure how much money they make from their core operations, like running a business, by removing certain costs or income that aren’t part of regular business activities. It helps investors see how well a company is doing without distractions from unusual expenses or gains, making it easier to compare companies or track performance over time.
book-to-bill ratiofinancial
The book-to-bill ratio compares the value of new orders a company receives to the value of products it ships out or bills for over a certain period. If the ratio is above 1, it means the company is getting more orders than it is completing, which can indicate growth. If it's below 1, it suggests demand is slowing down.
days sales outstandingfinancial
Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) measures the average number of days a company takes to collect payment after making a sale. It tells investors how quickly sales are turning into cash—shorter DSO means the company gets paid faster and has more cash on hand, while longer DSO suggests cash is tied up with customers and increases the risk of late or lost payments; think of it like how long a borrower takes to repay a loan.
non-gaapfinancial
Non-GAAP refers to financial measures that companies use to show their earnings or performance without including certain expenses or income that are often added back to give a different picture. It matters because it can make a company's results look better or more favorable, but it may also hide important costs, so investors need to look at both GAAP (official rules) and non-GAAP numbers to get a full understanding.

LONDON, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Brightstar Lottery PLC (NYSE:BRSL) ("Brightstar" or the "Company") today announced that Vince Sadusky, Chief Executive Officer ("CEO") and a member of the Brightstar Board of Directors, has elected to retire as CEO and from the Board of Directors on January 1, 2027.  Thomas Warsop, who was most recently Chief Executive Officer of ACI Worldwide Inc., has been appointed to succeed Vince Sadusky as CEO and will become a member of the Brightstar Board of Directors, in each case effective as of January 1, 2027.

"Our decision to appoint Thomas Warsop as Brightstar's new CEO reflects the outcome of a thorough succession process undertaken by our Board," said Marco Sala, Executive Chair of Brightstar.  "Tom has a demonstrated track record of creating value for stakeholders across numerous industries and competitive environments, including payments ecosystems, insurance, risk management, fintech, and technology. Importantly, Tom has extensive experience managing global teams with international operations and engaging with a global customer base." 

"I am excited to join the lottery industry's leader and build on the great foundation created by Brightstar's talented global team," said Thomas Warsop. "I look forward to working with stakeholders across our value chain to serve Brightstar's lottery customers around the world. I believe Brightstar is uniquely positioned to continue its transformation and deliver even greater value to customers and shareholders. I am energized by the opportunity here."

"On behalf of the Brightstar Board and all our employees across the globe, I would like to thank Vince for his significant contributions to Brightstar's success during his tenure as CEO," said Marco Sala. "Vince has had a role guiding this company and its predecessors since 2010 when he joined the IGT Board. After becoming CEO of Brightstar in 2022, he initiated a program to transform and evolve the Company. Most notably, Vince led the separation of our gaming and digital business which culminated in its sale to Apollo and during his tenure as CEO we returned more than $1.8 billion in capital to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. He also oversaw the design and implementation of new technologies and was a champion for innovation, organizational and AI-related initiatives. I am confident that his contribution will continue to deliver benefits to the company and its shareholders for years to come."

"I would like to thank the Board for their support of our strategies and initiatives. I also want to extend my deepest gratitude to the Brightstar team who provided their support, energy and dedication during my tenure as CEO. Working with them has been an incredibly rewarding experience for me personally," said Vince Sadusky, CEO of Brightstar.  "We have made great progress on Brightstar's strategy over the last five years and have assembled talented and motivated group that can continue to drive Brightstar's global leadership in the lottery industry."

About Thomas Warsop
Warsop served as CEO of ACI Worldwide Inc. from November 2022 to November 2026, and as a member of the ACI board of directors from June 2015 to November 2026. He has led various portfolio companies for several leading private equity firms, including One Call Care Management, York Risk Services Group, and The Warranty Group. He served as Group President at Fiserv, Inc., a provider of technology solutions to the financial industry, from 2007 to 2012. He served in various capacities at Electronic Data Systems for 17 years, including as President of its Business Process Outsourcing unit in Asia Pacific, Vice President in the United Kingdom, and Vice President of Global Financial Services.  He also serves as a member of the board of directors of Altus Group Limited (TSX:AIF).

VANCOUVER, BC, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Century Lithium Corp. (TSXV: LCE) (OTCQX: CYDVF) (Frankfurt: C1Z) ("Century Lithium" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that the U.S. Bureau of Land Management ("BLM"), Battle Mountain District, Tonopah Field Office, has determined that baseline data collection and reporting are complete for the Company's 100%-owned Angel Island Lithium Project ("Angel Island" or the "Project") in Esmeralda County, Nevada, USA. The BLM has also determined that the appropriate National Environmental Policy Act ("NEPA") review level for the Project is an Environmental Impact Statement ("EIS").

"This is a significant step for Angel Island. Having the BLM accept and confirm our baseline studies as complete reflects years of dedicated effort by our team, and puts the Project on the path to a Record of Decision," said Bill Willoughby, President and CEO of Century Lithium. "With the NEPA level of review now set, a clear federal process is established, and we are well positioned to move Angel Island forward as a key source of domestic lithium for the U.S. battery supply chain."

Baseline Completion and Acceptance

In a letter dated November 13, 2026, the BLM notified Century Lithium's wholly owned subsidiary, Cypress Holdings (Nevada), Ltd. ("Cypress"), that it had reviewed the baseline resource data submitted for the Project. The BLM determined that baseline data collection is complete for all resources its interdisciplinary team identified as relevant to the proposed action, including the additional baseline studies completed for the proposed water supply pipeline route and well field. This follows the BLM's earlier determination that the Mine Plan of Operations and Nevada Reclamation Permit Application ("PoO") for Angel Island is complete under 43 CFR § 3809.411 (see news release dated November 9, 2026).

NEPA Determination

In the same letter, the BLM determined that an EIS is the appropriate level of NEPA analysis for the Project. The EIS will be prepared in accordance with NEPA, the U.S. Department of the Interior's ("DOI") NEPA procedures at 43 CFR Part 46, and the DOI NEPA Handbook. The BLM will serve as lead agency for the federal environmental review. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, the Nevada Department of Wildlife, Esmeralda County, and Nye County have agreed to participate as cooperating agencies.

The proposed action under review includes an open pit, two overburden stockpiles, two low-grade ore stockpiles, a dry-stack tailings storage facility, roads, ancillary facilities (warehouse and office, shop, and laboratory), and a processing and leaching facility. The Project is designed for a projected mill feed of 5.5 million tonnes per year (at 15,000 tonnes per day), with estimated average annual production of 27,400 tonnes per year of lithium carbonate.

Next Steps Toward Environmental Review

With baseline studies accepted and the level of NEPA review set, the third-party NEPA contractor will continue preparation of the Supplemental Information Report, which will support development of the Supplemental Environmental Reports that form the basis of the EIS. Once the public scoping period and the NEPA analyses are complete, the PoO will be revised as needed for consistency, after which the BLM may issue a Record of Decision for the Project.

Permitting Timeline

Angel Island is a Transparency Project under the Federal Permitting Improvement Steering Council's FAST-41 program. The Permitting Dashboard for Federal Infrastructure Projects currently shows a target date of February 4, 2028, for issuance of the Record of Decision for the Project. As with any federal schedule, this timetable is subject to change as the review progresses, and the Company will provide updates as key milestones are reached.

Qualified Person

The scientific and technical information in this news release was reviewed and approved by Daniel W. Kalmbach, CPG, Vice President, Exploration and Resource Development of Century Lithium Corp., who is a non-independent Qualified Person as defined by National Instrument 43-101 - Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects.

All references to mining, processing and economics for Angel Island herein are from the Updated NI 43-101 Technical Report on the Feasibility Study of the Clayton Valley Lithium Project, Esmeralda County, Nevada, USA (the project is now known as Angel Island), with an effective date of January 3, 2026, which is available on SEDAR+ and the Company's website.

ABOUT CENTURY LITHIUM CORP.

Century Lithium Corp. is an advanced-stage lithium development company focused on its 100%-owned Angel Island Lithium Project in Esmeralda County, Nevada. Angel Island hosts one of the largest known sedimentary lithium deposits in the United States and is designed with an integrated, end-to-end process for the on-site production of battery-grade lithium carbonate to support the electric vehicle and battery storage markets.

The Company has developed a patent-pending process that incorporates hydrochloric acid leaching combined with direct lithium extraction to produce battery-grade lithium carbonate. As part of the integrated chlor-alkali process, Angel Island is designed to produce sodium hydroxide as a co-product, with planned surplus sales expected to lower operating costs, reduce reliance on externally sourced reagents, and minimize environmental impacts.

Century Lithium is currently advancing Angel Island through the permitting process.

Century Lithium trades on the TSX Venture Exchange under the symbol "LCE", on the OTCQX under the symbol "CYDVF", and on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange under the symbol "C1Z".

To learn more, please visit centurylithium.com.

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Cabral Gold Inc. (TSXV: CBR) (OTCQX: CBGZF) ("Cabral" or the "Company") is pleased to announce results from an independently prepared updated Mineral Resource Estimate ("MRE") for the Cuiú Cuiú project, Pará State, Brazil.

Highlights:

  • Total Measured and Indicated Resources are 42.5Mt @ 0.73 g/t gold (998,800 oz), while the total Inferred Resources are 82.1Mt @ 0.95 g/t gold (2,512,900 oz). The totals represent a 49% increase in Measured and Indicated Resources and a 376% increase in Inferred Resources on previous estimates
  • Open-pit oxide resources reported as part of the above total resources and amenable to heap-leach processing, are reported for all six deposits, containing total Measured and Indicated Resources of 21.6Mt @ 0.38 g/t gold (265,600 oz) and additional total Inferred Resources of 16.7Mt @ 0.39 g/t gold (210,900 oz)
  • In addition, open-pit resources for the underlying primary or hard rock mineralization and reported as part of the above total resources, comprise Indicated Resources of 20.8Mt @ 1.09 g/t gold (733,200 oz) and Inferred resources of 65.4Mt @ 1.09 g/t gold (2,302,000 oz). Resources are contained within six gold deposits, all of which remain open at depth
  • A significant amount of higher-grade primary material is contained within the current MRE. At a cut-off grade of 1.00 g/t gold, the primary, or hard rock resource comprises Indicated resources of 6.2Mt @ 2.32 g/t gold (463,200 oz) and Inferred resources of 19.1Mt @ 2.37 g/t gold (1,452,200 oz)
  • All six gold deposits remain open at depth and several deposits including Central, PDM, Machichie and Jerimum Cima remain open along strike. There are over 50 peripheral partially tested and untested targets at Cuiú Cuiú that contain gold

Alan Carter, Cabral's President and CEO commented, "The updated MRE for the Cuiú Cuiú district is a significant increase over the previous resource estimate and is another important milestone in the development of our project. Primary or hard resources have increased by 63% and now contain 733,200oz of gold in the Indicated category, whilst primary resources in the Inferred category have increased by 406% and now contain 2,302,000oz of gold since the previous resource estimate. Near surface oxide resources have also grown significantly over the previous resource estimate. Oxide resources in the Measured and Indicated category have expanded by 21% and now contain 265,600oz of gold, whilst oxide resources in the Inferred category have grown by 190% and now contain 210,900oz of gold. This growth in the oxide resource base is expected to have positive implications for expanding the Phase 1 heap leach operation in the near term."

"The Cuiú Cuiú project is beginning to exhibit its true potential and now ranks as one of the largest gold projects, and the second largest undeveloped primary gold deposit, in Brazil. It is the largest gold project in the Tapajós region of Pará state by a significant margin. All six of the deposits identified to date are open at depth, and several are open along strike. Over 50 peripheral targets with gold in reconnaissance drill holes, surface trenches and boulder fields at Cuiú Cuiú remain untested or partially tested. I would like to thank and congratulate the entire geological team on this very significant achievement."

Cuiú Cuiú Project

The Cuiú Cuiú Project is located within the Tapajós Gold District, approximately 195 kilometers ("km") south-southwest of Itaituba, within the state of Pará in northern Brazil. The Project is well connected to the BR-163 highway located 60km to the south-east by a network of recently upgraded roads. Cabral Gold has a 100 percent ("%") interest in a total of 30,563 hectares covering the district. Exploration to date has resulted in several discoveries including the six deposits mentioned herein (Figure 1) as well as 50+ additional targets currently under exploration.

Cabral is pursuing a two-phase development strategy at Cuiú Cuiú. Phase 1 is a 3000 tonne per day ("t/d") heap leach operation and open pit mine capable of mining and processing gold-in-oxide saprolite ore equivalent to 1 million tonnes ("Mt") per annum. The mine is ramping up to commercial production and announced its first gold pour on September 10, 2026. The Phase 2 development will focus on the much larger primary or hard rock resource. Both oxide and primary resources are updated as part of this press release.

Mineralization within the district is hosted primarily in granitic and dioritic intrusive rocks, in quartz stockwork and breccia zones surrounding high-grade veins filling linear subvertical structures. An upper zone of weathered and oxidized material averaging 60m in thickness from surface, highly amenable to heap leaching, overlies the primary intrusive-hosted gold mineralization.

Mineral Resource Estimate

The MRE covers six gold deposits within the central part of Cuiú Cuiú district: MG, Machichie, Central, PDM, JB and Jerimum Cima. Several other targets have economic drill intercepts including Morro da Lua, Machichie SW and Central SE, but currently have insufficient drilling to be included in the current MRE update.

Total resources are reported in terms of near surface oxide resources and primary or hard rock resources. Measured and Indicated Resources are 42.5Mt @ 0.73 g/t gold (998,800 ounces ("oz"), while the total Inferred Resources are 82.1Mt @ 0.95 g/t gold (2,512,900 oz) (see Table 1). The total resources represent a 49% increase in Measured and Indicated resources and a 376% increase in Inferred resources over the most recent previous resource estimates for oxide and primary resources.

Open-pit oxide resources amenable to heap-leach processing are reported for all six deposits, containing total Measured and Indicated resources of 21.6Mt @ 0.38 g/t gold (265,600 oz) and additional total Inferred resources of 16.7Mt @ 0.39 g/t gold (210,900 oz) (Table 1).

Mineral resources for the underlying primary or hard rock mineralization at Cuiú Cuiú comprise open pit Indicated resources of 20.8Mt @ 1.09 g/t gold (733,200 oz) and Inferred resources of 65.4Mt @ 1.09 g/t gold (2,302,000 oz) (Table 1). All of the six gold deposits included in this MRE remain open at depth and several deposits including Central, PDM, Machichie and Jerimum Cima remain open along strike.

Assumptions

Mineralization wireframes were initially generated in Leapfrog Geo using implicit modelling, based on composited gold assays at a nominal cut-off grade of 0.1 g/t Au and downhole structural measurements. Where necessary, the wireframes were subsequently refined in Micromine using conventional explicit modelling techniques, involving geological interpretation on cross-sections and subsequent linking of interpreted boundaries. Additional surfaces were constructed to delineate the boundaries between oxide and primary mineralization zones.

Block modelling was completed by VMG using Micromine software. The parent block size was 10 × 10 × 10 m, with sub-blocking to a minimum size of 1 × 1 × 1 m along wireframe boundaries. Gold grades were estimated using ordinary kriging, with search radii and search ellipse orientations determined through variographic analysis. Density values were interpolated using inverse distance squared (IDW2) where data quantity and spatial distribution were sufficient; otherwise, average density values were assigned.

VMG employed classical capping strategy to limit the influence of higher-grade outliers. Capping statistics were compiled for each deposit and each gold zone separately, resulting in assay top cuts or caps ranging from 2.5 g/t gold to 35.8 g/t gold.

All Inferred Resources, Indicated and Measured Resources are defined in accordance with the Canadian Institute of Mining, Metallurgy and Petroleum Definition Standards for Mineral Resources and Mineral Reserves (2014) (the "CIM Standards"). Mineral Resources were classified based on drill spacing, estimation parameters, geological continuity, and confidence in the geometry of the mineralized bodies. Measured Resources were defined in areas with a regular 25 × 25 m drill spacing, requiring a minimum of three drill holes and four composites, while Indicated Resources were defined in areas with 50 × 50 m or 100 × 50 m spacing, requiring at least two drill holes and two composites. Both categories were estimated using two-thirds of the search radius in their respective interpolation passes. The remaining estimated blocks were classified as Inferred Resources. Classification boundaries were defined using category-specific wireframes. Cabral corporate modelers and geologists reviewed the VMG models and created parallel validation models. Visual inspection of the block models versus the geology and assays was conducted by all parties.

Mineral Resources were calculated within Lerchs-Grossmann (LG) cones using MicroMine software considering open pit mining and a gold price of US$3,500/oz per ounce. The Company is continuing with aggressive drilling programs in terms of exploration and also resource development. A significant amount of infill drilling is planned for 2027 in order to upgrade the Inferred portion of the MRE.

Several of the gold deposits at Cuiú Cuiú, including Jerimum Cima, Machichie, Central and PDM remain open along strike, and all of the deposits identified to date are open at depth. Drilling over the next few months will also target potential extensions to the known deposits.

The Company has also initiated work on the potential to add additional near surface oxide resources amenable to heap leach processing, and also to upgrade the Inferred resources to the Measured and Indicated category.

Dr. Myadzel is independent of the Company and has verified the data disclosed including sampling, analytical, and test data underlying the drill results, using a variety of techniques including comparison against independently sourced assay certificates, site visit investigations, and digital based verification tests, and consents to the inclusion in this release of said data in the form and context in which it appears. Dr. Myadzel experienced no limitations with respect to data verification activities related to the Cuiu Cuiu project.

Technical information included in this release was supervised and approved by Brian Arkell, B.S. Geology and M.S. Economic Geology, SME (Registered Member), AusIMM (Fellow) and SEG (Fellow), Cabral Gold's Vice President, Technical Services, and a Qualified Person under NI 43-101. Mr. Arkell has verified the data disclosed including sampling, analytical, and test data underlying the drill results, using a variety of techniques including implementing quality assurance/quality control ("QA/QC") sampling measures, review and validation of the geological models, and review of the geostatistical approaches in the Mineral Resource estimation.

Technical Report

Further details supporting the technical and scientific information outlined herein, including the geological model, estimation procedure and block modelling will be available in a National Instrument 43-101 Technical Report authored by Volodymyr Myadzel, PhD, MAIG, of VMG Consultoria e Soluções Ltda. of Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais, Brazil. The report will be posted under the Cabral profile at www.sedarplus.ca within 45 days from the date of this news release.

About Cabral Gold Inc.

The Company is a junior gold mining company engaged in the exploration, development and production from gold properties located in Brazil. The Company has a 100% interest in the Cuiú Cuiú gold district located in the Tapajós Region, within the state of Pará in northern Brazil. Six main gold deposits have so far been defined at the Cuiú Cuiú project which contain National Instrument ("NI") 43-101 compliant Measured and Indicated Resources of 21.6Mt @ 0.38 g/t gold (265,600 oz) and Inferred Resources of 16.7Mt @ 0.39 g/t gold (210,900 oz) in oxide material. The project also contains Indicated resources of 20.8Mt @ 1.09 g/t gold (733,200 oz) and Inferred resources of 65.4Mt @ 1.09 g/t gold (2,302,000 oz) of primary or hard rock material. The resource estimate is based on a press release dated November 19, 2026 and a NI 43-101 technical report is expected to be filed within 45 days of this date. Award-winning land-and-sea journeys take guests deeper into Alaska and Canada, from Denali National Park to the Yukon

SEATTLE, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Bookings are open for Holland America Line's 2028 Alaska Cruisetour season, giving guests their first opportunity to pair an overland journey into the Great Land with a cruise aboard the reimagined Oosterdam. Following its Holland America Evolution transformation, Oosterdam will make its Alaska debut in 2028, bringing new onboard experiences to a Cruisetour program that combines the coast with deeper exploration into Alaska's interior.

Holland America Line opens 2028 Alaska Cruisetours, pairing reimagined Oosterdam with journeys into Alaska's interior.

The 2028 season comes as Holland America Line celebrates two new awards distinguishing its place as a leader in Alaska vacations. U.S. News & World Report named Holland America the No. 1 Best Cruise Line in Alaska. U.S. News said Holland America earned the number one ranking this week because of "its extensive regional itineraries, decades of sailing experience, coveted Glacier Bay permits and 'Glacier Guarantee.'" And Holland America Line's 12-Day Signature Denali Cruisetour was named a winner in Good Housekeeping's Travel Awards. In its award summary, Good Housekeeping cited the ability to explore on land and sea, renovations to Holland America Denali Lodge and amazing glacier views.

Guests can choose from 19 Cruisetours itineraries aboard four ships, ranging from nine to 17 days operating between May and September. Each experience combines an Alaska cruise with an overland journey that includes a stay at the newly transformed Holland America Denali Lodge, following completion of its $70 million multi-year enhancement project in 2027. At the doorstep of Denali National Park & Preserve, the lodge will offer guests refreshed accommodations and public spaces, expanded dining experiences and other property enhancements. Each Cruisetour also includes a tour into the park and travel through Alaska's interior by rail and motorcoach.

"One of the things that makes Alaska so extraordinary is how different it looks from the water and from the interior—guests sail past glaciers and rugged coastlines, then journey inland to the mountains and wide-open landscapes of Denali National Park," said Dan Rough, vice president of revenue management for Holland America Line. "A Cruisetour brings everything together, and after generations of exploring Alaska, Holland America Line has the experience to help guests see more of the Great Land in one journey. We also are excited to add the reimagined Oosterdam to our Cruisetour lineup in 2028."

Classic, Signature and Ultimate Alaska & Denali Cruisetours pair the overland experience with a 7-Day Glacier Discovery cruise aboard Oosterdam or Eurodam, while Alaska, Denali & Yukon Cruisetours travel farther into Canada's Yukon Territory with either a 7-Day Glacier Discovery cruise or a shorter Alaska Inside Passage cruise aboard Koningsdam or Zaandam. Holland America Line is the only cruise line to take guests into the Yukon on a Cruisetour, traveling beyond Skagway to Whitehorse and Dawson City.

Experience Alaska from Ship to Interior
Highlights for 2028 include:

  • Holland America Evolution comes to Alaska: For the first time, guests can experience Holland America Evolution in Alaska aboard Oosterdam. The reimagined ship features purpose-built Solo Verandah staterooms, Bridgeview Suites with panoramic forward-facing views, Grand Dutch Café, refreshed accommodations and updated guest spaces, bringing the cruise line's largest fleet investment in its 153-year history to a destination where Holland America Line has long been a leader.
  • Holland America Denali Lodge at the doorstep of Denali National Park: Every Cruisetour includes a stay at Holland America Denali Lodge. Guests in 2028 will experience Holland America Denali Lodge following completion of its $70 million multi-year enhancement project, including two new guest buildings adding 72 rooms, refreshed public spaces and expanded dining experiences. Included tours take guests into Denali National Park & Preserve. Two- and three-night stays at Holland America Denali Lodge include the Tundra Wilderness Tour, while one-night stays include the Denali Natural History Tour.
  • Alaska by rail and motorcoach: Every Cruisetour includes travel aboard the glass-domed McKinley Explorer, with panoramic views, an open-air viewing platform, onboard commentary and dining. Holland America Line's owned railcars, motorcoaches and properties help connect each stage of the overland experience. Select itineraries also feature the historic White Pass & Yukon Route Railway and Direct-to-Denali service, taking guests from ship to Holland America Denali Lodge in a single day.
  • Alaska flavors and experiences ashore: At Holland America Denali Lodge, guests can experience destination programming at Denali Square, Music of Denali dinner theater and dining inspired by Alaska and the Pacific Northwest. Recent enhancements throughout Holland America Denali Lodge include expanded culinary offerings, updated menus and dining venues.
  • Go farther into the Yukon: Holland America Line is the only cruise line that takes guests into the heart of the Yukon on a Cruisetour, traveling beyond Skagway along the historic Klondike Gold Rush route to Whitehorse and Dawson City. In 2028, guests can explore Dawson City as the destination marks its 130th anniversary, with select itineraries including two nights at the Holland America Dawson City Inn, the Klondike Gold Tour and travel aboard the White Pass & Yukon Route Railway.

Four Ways to Experience Alaska by Land and Sea
The 2028 season offers four Cruisetour styles, giving guests options based on the length and type of overland experience: 

  • Classic Alaska & Denali Cruisetours: Three nine- to 10-day itineraries combine a 7-Day Glacier Discovery cruise with one night at Holland America Denali Lodge and the Denali Natural History Tour into Denali National Park & Preserve.
  • Signature Alaska & Denali Cruisetours: Six 10- to 12-day itineraries combine a 7-Day Glacier Discovery cruise with two or three nights at Holland America Denali Lodge and the Tundra Wilderness Tour into Denali National Park & Preserve.
  • Ultimate Alaska & Denali Cruisetours: Three 14-day itineraries combine a 7-Day Glacier Discovery cruise, two nights at Holland America Denali Lodge and an extended stay in Alyeska, Homer or Seward. Each features a dedicated Tour Director on land and an included visit to the Alaska Wildlife Conservation Center, along with additional included experiences depending on the itinerary, such as the Tundra Wilderness Tour, Riverboat Discovery and Gold Dredge 8.
  • Alaska, Denali & Yukon Cruisetours: Seven itineraries ranging from nine to 17 days offer a fully escorted overland experience, with a dedicated Tour Director accompanying guests throughout the land portion of the journey and providing local insight along the way. Each includes a stay at Holland America Denali Lodge, an included Denali National Park experience and exploration of the Yukon. Depending on the itinerary, guests pair their overland journey with either a 7-Day Glacier Discovery cruise aboard Oosterdam or Eurodam or a shorter Alaska Inside Passage cruise aboard Koningsdam or Zaandam.

Have It All Early Booking Bonus and Free Dining Package
For a limited time, guests who book 2028 Cruisetours with the Have It All Early Booking Bonus receive the Cruisetour Dining Package for the land portion of their journey, a $869-per-person value that extends more of the inclusive cruise experience ashore. The package includes select meals at Holland America properties during the overland journey, as well as lunch aboard the McKinley Explorer. Depending on the itinerary, guests can also enjoy dining associated with Music of Denali and the Tundra Wilderness Tour.

Additionally, the Have It All Early Booking Bonus includes shore excursion credit, specialty dining, an upgrade to Elite Beverage Package, an upgrade to Premium Wi-Fi, prepaid Crew Appreciation and the cruise line's Best Price Guarantee.

For more information about Holland America Line's shore excursions or to book a cruise, consult a travel advisor, call 1-877-SAIL HAL (877-724-5425) or visit hollandamerica.com.

Holland America Line has been exploring the world for more than 150 years with expertly crafted itineraries, extraordinary service and genuine connections to the destinations. Offering a perfectly-sized ship experience, its fleet of 11 vessels visits nearly 400 ports in 114 countries around the world and has shared the thrill of Alaska for nearly 80 years — longer than any other cruise line. Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Tower Resources Ltd. (TSXV: TWR) ("Tower" or the "Company") is pleased to report assay results from 38 grab samples1 of boulders and outcropping or subcropping bedrock collected on the Rabbit North property in October within a 400-m-wide corridor straddling the fertile ENE structural trend between the Blue Sky Zone (see Fig. 1) and the 1001-grain gold-in-till anomaly previously identified 800 m to the northeast near the center of the Durand Stock (see November 3, 2025 press release).

Strong Au assays up to 15.1 g/t were obtained from four boulder samples along the Blue Sky structural trend (see Fig. 2), confirming that its fertility is sustained to the middle of the Durand Stock. A bedrock outcrop 250 m down-ice from the 1001-grain anomaly, apparently on the parallel Lightning trend, returned 8.06 g/t Au and 0.62% Cu supported by 0.79 and 0.31 g/t Au values from two nearby bedrock subcrops, effectively doubling the gold potential of the central part of the stock.



Figure 1 - Location of the Rabbit North property showing the current survey area relative to the geology of the central part and the major shear structures controlling Tower's gold discoveries. These shear zones are roughly coincident with more recent graben fault valleys that have been infilled by Chilcotin basalt flows. The yellow stars mark the locations of the main Au intersections in the initial discovery holes on the gold zones.

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:
https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/5023/324830_figure1.jpg



Figure 2 - Locations of significantly mineralized (>0.3 g/t Au) boulder and bedrock samples relative to the Blue Sky and Lightning trends and the gold grain content of the glacial till cover.

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:
https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/5023/324830_figure2.jpg

Sampling Program

In early October, the Company performed three days of geological mapping and boulder prospecting in a 400 x 800 m area straddling the northeastern trajectory of the Blue Sky shear trend as inferred from the abundance of gold grains in the overlying glacial till (see Fig. 2). Information was recorded at 105 sites, including small, previously unmapped outcrops and rubbly subcrops that help constrain the trajectories of the fertile gold structures.

The possibility of finding intact mineralized boulders was limited because the tops of the shear zones were recessively oxidized to soft, clayey saprolite prior to glaciation. In addition, the westernmost 200 m of the shear trend is covered by younger Chilcotin basalt flows and was not glaciated. Nevertheless, 27 rusty boulders, many either stabilized by resistant quartz veins (see Fig. 3a) or reduced to a residual quartz boxwork (see Fig. 3b) by leaching of their original sulphides, were found and analyzed, along with three samples from outcropping bedrock and eight from subcrop.

Figure 3 (a) and (b) - Intensely oxidized boulders from preglacially saprolitized gold zones. 



a) Boulder 246, 3.03 g/t Au, ~50 m down-ice from the Blue Sky Trend near the 1001 grain gold anomaly in the till. Vuggy, sulphide-depleted quartz veins in indecipherable, saprolitized host rock. 

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:
https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/5023/324830_41df4844d434480a_003full.jpg



b) Bouder 294, 0.72 g/t Au, ~100 m down-ice from the Blue Sky Trend. Former sulphides have been completely leached out, leaving a honeycomb-like boxwork of resistate quartz. Original Au content may have been significantly higher.

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:
https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/5023/324830_41df4844d434480a_004full.jpg

Au Results from Blue Sky Trend

Four distinctly auriferous boulders containing from 0.72 to 15.1 g/t Au (see Table 1) were found east of the Blue Sky Zone along the two untested segments of the structural trend that are not covered by Chilcotin basalt and thus were glaciated (see Fig. 2).

Boulder No. 327a with 2.40 g/t Au is roughly coincident with a 292-grain till gold anomaly astride the structural trend where it emerges from basalt cover ~100 m east along strike from the most easterly Blue Sky drill holes. A bedrock sample, No. 330 from an outcrop ~50 m further east, returned 1.86 g/t Au. Together these results imply that the Blue Sky Zone is at least twice its currently defined 150 m length.

The two most strongly mineralized of the other three boulders were found 500 m further east along the Blue Sky trend close to the peak 1001-grain gold anomaly. The sample from Boulder 246, ~50 from the till sample site, yielded 3.03 g/t Au and 73.5 g/t (2.14 oz/ton) Ag. The boulder contains residual quartz veins (see Fig. 3a) but is too oxidized to allow identification of the host rock. No bedrock exposures are present nearby. A smaller block of rusty diorite with vuggy, pyrite-depleted quartz veins (not photographed) found ~150 m down-ice from (southeast of) the Blue Sky trend, Boulder 251, yielded a highlight 15.1 g/t Au assay.

The fourth boulder, No. 294 midway along the Blue Sky trend (see Fig. 2), yielded only 0.72 g/t Au and 11.2 g/t Ag but is completely depleted of its formerly abundant sulphides (see Fig. 3b) and thus may be derived from a mineralized zone having a significantly higher primary Au content.

Au Results from Lightning Trend

Mapping and sampling of the available bedrock exposures along the southern edge of the survey area resulted in shifting the eastern trajectory of the Lightning structure to this area (see Fig. 2) from its previously inferred position ~300 m to the south.

One of the narrow, ENE trending features within the Durand Stock (grey lenses in Fig. 1) that were historically mapped as felsite dykes but are now known to be sheared and QSP altered diorite ± quartz-feldspar porphyry was sampled (No. 286 in Fig. 2) and returned 0.72 g/t Au, extending the Lightning Zone structural trend 600 m ENE from the drill defined gold zone.
