Final assays from 2026 RC Program Continue to Expand Deposit's Dimensions

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - North Arrow Minerals Inc. (TSXV: NAR) (OTCQB: NHAWF) (FSE: 9TB) ("North Arrow" or the "Company") today reports results from the final seven of sixteen reverse circulation ("RC") holes completed during Rotation 4 at the Kraaipan Gold Project ("Kraaipan") in southern Botswana. Five holes were drilled at Tlou (Target AE): one infill hole and one step-out to the north, one deeper hole testing the down-dip extent of mineralization, and two scissor holes to help define its geometry. All five intersected gold mineralization with four intersecting broad zones of mineralization comparable to earlier 2026 results at Tlou. Two holes at Nkwe (Target AF) tested the southern extension of Grid 1 and intersected narrow zones of mineralization.

With these results, all 14 Rotation 4 holes at Tlou have intersected gold mineralization. North Arrow drilling has now traced the mineralized trend over approximately 750 metres of strike, from KR26-099 in the south to KR26-102 in the north, and historical drilling by previous operators intersected the same favourable contact a further 200 m to the south. Mineralization at Tlou remains open along strike and at depth.

Key Highlights

  • Consistent, broad mineralization along close to one kilometre of strike - Rotation 4 drilling has returned wide zones of gold mineralization from surface along the Tlou trend, including 1.17 g/t Au over 42 m in KR26-095 (reported November 4, 2026) and 0.63 g/t Au over 48 m in KR26-108 (reported today).
  • KR26-108 infill hole returns 0.63 g/t Au over 48 m from 20 m depth, including 0.91 g/t Au over 23 m. KR26-108 was drilled between KR26-043 (0.57 g/t Au over 35 m) and KR26-100 (0.36 g/t Au over 45 m).
  • Deepest hole at Tlou ends in mineralization - KR26-105 returned 0.57 g/t Au over 15 m from 121 m down hole, including 1.68 g/t Au over the final 2 m, extending mineralization to more than 100 m vertical depth. Quartz veining with fresh pyrite was logged at the end of the hole.
  • Scissor holes support a steep to sub-vertical geometry - KR26-107 returned 0.64 g/t Au over 26 m, including 0.96 g/t Au over 14 m, and KR26-106 returned 0.48 g/t Au over 27 m, including 0.96 g/t Au over 7 m.
  • Gold is not restricted to banded iron formation - much of the higher-grade interval in KR26-108 lies within a unit logged as altered possible mafic rock interbedded with approximately equal proportions of ferruginous chert. Together with earlier results in altered mafic rocks and hematite-altered iron-rich rocks, this enhances the understanding of gold mineralization associations with the KGB and will assist in effective targeting.

CEO Commentary

Eira Thomas, Chief Executive Officer of North Arrow, stated:

"Tlou continues to develop into a coherent discovery. Every hole we have drilled on this trend in Rotation 4 has intersected zones of gold mineralization, and our drilling now traces those zones over approximately 750 metres, within a trend of close to one kilometre that remains open along strike and at depth. Our deepest hole ended in mineralization, and we are seeing gold in what are possibly mafic rocks as well as in banded iron formation, which deepens our understanding of gold mineralization associations within the Kraaipan Greenstone Belt. Broad zones of gold associated with BIF, quartz veining and pyrite are characteristic of Harmony's Kalgold mine, 40 kilometres to the south, and that is the model we are now testing. We finish 2026 with three discoveries - Tlou, Nkwe and Tau - and a clear set of targets for core drilling in 2027."

Drilling Summary

Sixteen RC drill holes, totalling 1,075 m were completed during Rotation 4: 14 at Tlou (968 m) and two at Nkwe (107 m). Results for the first nine holes, all at Tlou, were reported on November 4, 2026. Table 1 summarizes all 16 holes, Figure 1 shows the locations of the three discoveries, Figure 2 shows hole locations at Tlou and Table 2 summarizes assay results for the seven holes reported today.

Tlou RC Drilling Results

Five holes reported today complete the 14-hole Tlou program. The program was designed to test the northern and southern strike extent of the mineralization first drilled in May 2026 (see news release dated July 15, 2026), to test its down-dip extent and to help resolve its geometry (Figures 2 and 3).

Figure 2: Tlou Rotation 4 RC drill holes, select results

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:

Tlou North

KR26-108 was drilled as an infill hole between KR26-043 (0.57 g/t Au over 35 m, including 1.72 g/t Au over 7 m) and KR26-100 (0.36 g/t Au over 45 m). It returned 0.63 g/t Au over 48 m from 20 m down hole, including 0.91 g/t Au over 23 m, consistent with the wide intervals in neighbouring holes. Much of the 23-metre interval lies within a unit logged altered possible mafic rock interbedded with approximately equal proportions of ferruginous chert.

KR26-102 was collared 60 m north of KR26-101 and returned 0.31 g/t Au over 10 m, including 0.51 g/t Au over 2 m. The hole confirms that the mineralized system continues northward. The footwall rock package becomes more varied to the north, and the sand cover in this area means the full package may not yet have been tested.

Tlou Main: down-dip and scissor holes

KR26-105 was drilled from the east to test mineralization below KR26-039 and KR26-040 (1.11 g/t Au over 27 m). It returned 0.57 g/t Au over 15 m from 121 m down hole, including 1.68 g/t Au over the final 2 m, and ended in mineralization at 136 m. The interval lies approximately 105-118 m below surface, the deepest mineralization intersected at Tlou to date. The lower part of the hole intersected chert-rich BIF with dense quartz veining, chlorite alteration and disseminated pyrite. Mineralization remains open at depth.

KR26-106 and KR26-107 were drilled from the west as scissor holes. Both passed through variably altered and sheared mafic rocks before intersecting altered ferruginous chert and BIF. KR26-107 returned 0.64 g/t Au over 26 m, including 0.96 g/t Au over 14 m, and KR26-106 returned 0.48 g/t Au over 27 m, including 0.96 g/t Au over 7 m. Together with KR26-105, these holes indicate that the mineralized zone is steep to sub-vertical, or dips steeply west, at this location (Figure 3). Logging suggests locally thickening of the alteration and veining, and further work is needed to define these controls.

Figure 3: Cross-section through KR26-105, KR26-106 and KR26-107, looking north. Hole traces assume -60 dip, lithology from RC chip logging, intersections are not true widths

Gold in Multiple Host Rocks

BIF and ferruginous chert remain the primary exploration target at Kraaipan, as they are at Kalgold. Drilling at Tlou now shows that gold also occurs in other rock types:

  • Mafic rocks: much of the 0.91 g/t Au over 23 m interval in KR26-108 lies within a unit comprising a mixture of altered possible mafic rock and ferruginous chert. KR26-095 returned 0.84 g/t Au over 4 m from an altered, quartz-veined mafic unit (November 4, 2026).
  • Iron-rich, hematite-altered rocks: KR26-100 returned 0.56 g/t Au over 16 m from a massive, hematite-altered, variably magnetic unit with no discernible quartz veining.
  • Quartz veins: outcropping northwest-trending quartz veins with shallow to moderate northeast dips cut the north-trending stratigraphy. Gold is associated with these veins and their altered selvages in drill holes, and in surface samples at Tlou, Nkwe and Tau (Aug 24 2026, July 15 2026, April 16 2026, Feb 27,2026).

Fresh pyrite in KR26-105 confirms the association of sulphides with altered vein selvages and with silicified, iron-flooded ferruginous chert and BIF. The presence of quartz veining, sulphides and potentially replacement-style alteration in other altered rocks (possibly mafics) expands the potential host units for mineralization beyond BIF and ferruginous chert. These observations assist in better understanding the gold associations and will inform future targeting. The relationship between mineralization in non-BIF units and the regional structure will be a focus of mapping and geochemical interpretation.

Nkwe RC Drilling

Two holes were drilled south of Grid 1 at Nkwe to test the strike extent of mineralization intersected in KR26-021 (4.04 g/t Au over 9 m; see news release dated July 15, 2026). KR26-104 returned 0.96 g/t Au over 2 m and KR26-103 returned 0.44 g/t Au over 1 m, both in narrow zones of altered, quartz-veined ferruginous chert and foliated mafic rock, extending near-surface mineralization at Nkwe to more than [550] metres of strike.

2026 Exploration Budget

As previously reported, the 2026 exploration budget was increased from US$2.3 million to US$2.86 million to accommodate Rotation 4 drilling, expanded rock sampling and new soil sampling grids.

Next Steps

  • Interpretation of Tlou results and planning of a 2027 core drilling program to test the geometry, continuity and depth extent of mineralization.
  • Integration of RC results into regional targeting, incorporating the improved understanding of the gold associations generated from 2026 results.
  • Hyperspectral scanning of representative 2025 and 2026 RC chips was completed in early Q4 2026; results are being compiled.
  • Surface prospecting, soil sampling and ground geophysics will continue across the property.

About the Kraaipan Gold Project

The Kraaipan Project comprises approximately 724 km² of mineral concessions covering the entire ~60 km northern extension of the Kraaipan Greenstone Belt, a highly prospective Archean greenstone terrain straddling the Botswana-South Africa border. Over 80% of the northern portion of the belt is covered by Kalahari overburden, which has seen limited past exploration. The South African portion of the belt hosts numerous mineral occurrences including Harmony Gold's Kalgold Mine, a multi-million-ounce, BIF-hosted gold operation located 40 km to the south that has been in continuous production for over 30 years. Mineralization at Kalgold is not necessarily indicative of mineralization on the Kraaipan Project.

North Arrow can earn up to 80% interest in the Kraaipan Project from Rockman Resources through a First Option to earn 60% by investing US$5 M over three years (US$1 M firm commitment achieved), and a Second Option, at Rockman's election, to earn an additional 20% upon completion of a Preliminary Economic Assessment. North Arrow's partner Rockman Resources - through its operator Mineral Services - leverages over 25 years of operational experience in Botswana, together with proprietary technologies including high-resolution UAV magnetics, a mobile RC drilling platform optimized for Kalahari conditions, and in-house sample preparation.

Sampling, Laboratory Analyses and QA/QC

RC and surface rock samples collected in the field were driven to Mineral Services' facility in Gaborone to be sorted and prioritized for assay. Samples were allocated unique random sample numbers, sealed and shipped to ALS's laboratory in Johannesburg, South Africa using industry-standard chain-of-custody protocols. Following an initial coarse crush (CRU-21), the entire sample is then pulverized (PUL-21) to better than 85% passing a 75-micron screen prior to geochemical analysis. All samples are analyzed for gold by fire assay with an ICP-AES finish, method code Au-ICP22 (50-gram sample). Samples returning gold values over 10 ppm are subjected to ore-grade check assays using fire assay and a gravimetric finish using method code Au-GRA22 (50-gram sample). Samples are also subjected to lithium borate fusion and acid digestion for whole-rock analysis of major and trace elements by ICP-AES (major elements) and ICP-MS (trace elements); method codes ME-ICP06 and ME-MS81, respectively. In addition, a suite of base metals and other trace elements not included in the ME-MS81 method are analysed by ICP-AES on four-acid digestions (method code ME-4ACD81).

QA/QC protocols include ALS laboratory's own internal quality assurance controls as well as Rockman's field controls, including the insertion of duplicates and certified reference materials (CRM), each at a rate of roughly one per 20 samples. QA/QC data are evaluated on receipt for failures, and appropriate action is taken if results for duplicates, CRMs and blanks fall outside allowed tolerances.

About North Arrow Minerals

North Arrow Minerals is a Vancouver-based exploration company focused on evaluating the Kraaipan Gold Project. Management and advisors bring significant global exploration and mining experience. Reflects Strengthening Financial Profile, Strong Cash Flow Generation, Successful Balance Sheet De-Leveraging Below 3x, and Confidence in Continued Momentum

INDIANAPOLIS, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Elanco Animal Health Incorporated (NYSE: ELAN) announced today its Board of Directors has authorized the repurchase of up to $600 million of the company's common stock. The authorization reflects Elanco's accelerating operational momentum, robust free cash flow generation, strengthened balance sheet and clear path to net leverage ratio of 2.0 to 2.5 times.

After reaching the targeted sub 3.0x net leverage ratio, the company is updating its capital allocation priorities. Elanco will remain focused on a combination of debt paydown and accretive growth opportunities including continued investment in innovation, while starting a multi-year share repurchase program to drive enhanced, long-term shareholder value.

"Today's authorization of our first-ever share repurchase program reflects Elanco's financial transformation into a consistent, reliable growth company with more than three years of steady quarterly growth," said Jeff Simmons, President and CEO of Elanco. "Our disciplined execution against our Innovation, Portfolio and Productivity (IPP) strategy and expectations of a multi-year runway of mid-single digit revenue growth, high single digit adjusted EBITDA growth and low double digit adjusted EPS growth give us the financial flexibility to accelerate capital return to shareholders, while continuing to fully fund our growth priorities and pipeline to ensure a consistent flow of high-impact innovation."

Over the past several years, Elanco has prioritized debt reduction, successfully reducing its net leverage ratio (NLR) by approximately three-quarters of a turn in 2026 year-to-date alone. Earlier this month, the company reported a major strategic milestone as NLR fell below 3.0x faster than anticipated, unlocking accelerated capital allocation flexibility.

"Our continued strong operational performance and momentum achieving sub-3.0x leverage ahead of schedule gives us confidence to transition to a more balanced capital allocation framework," said Bob VanHimbergen, Executive Vice President and CFO of Elanco. "My priority is driving down costs through Elanco Ascend and general and administrative expenses to compensate for inflation. While there is still more to do, we're pleased with the team's disciplined execution to improve working capital management. We're tracking ahead of schedule toward our cumulative free cash flow target of $1 billion from 2026 to 2028, with free cash flow reaching $362 million as of the end of the third quarter and making continued progress toward our long-term margin goals."

The timing, manner and amount of repurchases will depend on a variety of factors, including market conditions, stock price, alternative capital deployment opportunities, and applicable regulatory requirements. The program does not obligate the company to acquire any specific dollar amount or number of shares and may be modified, suspended, or discontinued at any time without prior notice.

About Elanco
Elanco Animal Health Incorporated (NYSE: ELAN) is a global leader in animal health dedicated to innovating and delivering products and services to prevent and treat disease in farm animals and pets, creating value for farmers, pet owners, veterinarians, stakeholders and society as a whole. With 70 years of animal health heritage, we are committed to breaking boundaries and going beyond to help our customers improve the health of animals in their care, while also making a meaningful impact on our local and global communities. At Elanco, we are driven by our vision of Food and Companionship Enriching Life and our purpose – all to Go Beyond for Animals, Customers, Society and Our People. Learn more at www.elanco.com.
